mcq.q: Which belongs in a metric label?
mcq.why: Labels must be low-cardinality; IDs and prompts belong in traces or logs.

mcq.q: Which describes a trace?
options: The path of one request as a tree of timed spans linked by a trace ID
mcq.why: Traces propagate across services, queues and agents.

mcq.q: Metrics are cheap to store and alert on, but lack…
mcq.why: Use traces and logs for detail.

mcq.q: How does trace context cross a queue?
options: Put it in the message metadata so async work joins the same trace
mcq.why: The W3C traceparent header covers HTTP; queues need explicit metadata.

mcq.q: What does the OpenTelemetry Collector do?
options: Receives telemetry, processes it (sample, redact, enrich) and exports it to backends
mcq.why: It is a pipeline between services and backends.

mcq.q: Why must telemetry export use bounded queues and a drop policy?
options: So a slow telemetry backend never blocks requests or exhausts memory
mcq.why: Count what gets dropped.

mcq.q: What does a correlation ID do?
options: Links logs, spans, database rows and tickets for one request or task
mcq.why: The trace ID usually serves this role.

mcq.q: Using user IDs or prompts as metric labels causes…
mcq.why: Each unique label value creates a new series.

mcq.q: Which format do OTel exporters use to send data to backends?
mcq.why: Standard format lets you switch backends.

mcq.q: Which logs are easiest to query?
mcq.why: Consistent fields let you filter and join.

mcq.q: Error rate 1.5% against a 99.9% SLO gives a burn rate of…
mcq.why: 1.5% ÷ 0.1% = 15× (above the 14.4× paging threshold).

mcq.q: What should alerts fire on?
options: Symptoms users feel (SLO burn), not every cause
mcq.why: Each alert links to a runbook.

mcq.q: At a burn rate of 14.4, how long does a 30-day error budget last?
Error rate 0.5% against a 99.5% SLO. What is the burn rate?
mcq.why: 0.5% / 0.5% = 1, so the budget lasts exactly the window.

mcq.q: Why use multiple burn-rate windows?
options: A slow leak never trips the fast rule but drains the budget
Because one window is not allowed
mcq.why: Fast page, slow page and ticket rules.

mcq.q: Choose all the things a runbook should include.
options: What the alert means and how to confirm it
Escalation contacts and how to verify recovery
First mitigations: flags, rollbacks, degradation, failover
mcq.why: Runbooks make alerts actionable.

mcq.q: Where should an incident investigation start?
options: From affected traces linked from metrics, compared with healthy ones, plus recent changes
mcq.why: Check deploys, prompt, model and index versions and provider status.

mcq.q: What makes a postmortem blameless?
options: It focuses on systems and causes, not on punishing people
mcq.why: Action items have owners, including new evaluation cases and alerts.

mcq.q: What should dashboards annotate?
options: Deploys, model changes and config changes
mcq.why: Annotations turn charts into investigations.

mcq.q: An alert has no owner and no mitigation. What is it?
mcq.why: Every alert needs both.

mcq.q: HTTP success is 99.98% but grounded answers fell for one language. Which signal caught it?
mcq.why: Transport health cannot see answer quality.

mcq.q: Which is an implicit success signal?
options: The user did not rephrase or open a ticket afterwards
mcq.why: Implicit signals come from behaviour.

mcq.q: Why is “rephrase within 60 seconds” useful?
options: It correlates with unhelpful answers and is available immediately
mcq.why: It needs only logs and an embedding similarity check.

mcq.q: Escalations to humans suddenly fall. What could it mean?
options: The assistant may have become overconfident
mcq.why: Both too high and suddenly too low are signals.

mcq.q: Choose all the retrieval-failure signals the chapter lists.
mcq.why: Retrieval failures often precede quality complaints.

mcq.q: A model-provider update on day 9 shows up as…
options: Rising schema failures and falling groundedness
mcq.why: The dashboard caught it before users complained.

mcq.q: How should groundedness be monitored in production?
options: Judges on a continuous sample, tracked by feature, tenant and language
mcq.why: Sampled evaluation (8.2).

mcq.q: Is the agent saying “complete” a verified task-success label?
options: No; use outcome events or verification
mcq.why: Self-reports are not evidence.

mcq.q: Which are agent-specific signals?
options: Steps per task, loop-detector triggers and budget exhaustion rate
mcq.why: They show runaway behaviour.

mcq.q: Which signals belong under safety?
options: Guardrail block rate, injection-classifier hits and user reports
mcq.why: Track them alongside quality.

interview.q: Which AI-specific signals would you monitor beyond operational health?
What are explicit and implicit feedback signals?

covers: answers can be wrong but 200 OK

mcq.q: Choose all the things an AI trace should let you answer for one request.
options: Which tools ran with what arguments and results
Which prompt version and model were used
mcq.why: Also timings, tokens and cost, and what the user did next.

mcq.q: BM25 and vector search run in parallel. Which is on the critical path?
mcq.why: Only the slower parallel branch delays the request.
distractors: The faster one waits for nothing.

mcq.q: Critical path: rewrite 400, max(BM25 40, vector 60), rerank 800, model 850, tool 240, model 2,900 ms, run in sequence. What is the total?
Speeding up a span that is not on the critical path…
mcq.why: Speed up the longest span on the critical path.

mcq.q: Users say the assistant is slow on Mondays. What did the traces show in the chapter's example?
options: Rerank waiting for a GPU shared with the Monday ingestion backfill
mcq.why: That led to separating the reranker pool (15.3).

mcq.q: A worker starts a new unrelated trace. What breaks?
options: The causal chain: you cannot connect its work to the original request
mcq.why: Propagate context, or link child traces to the parent task.

mcq.q: How do multi-agent runs appear in tracing?
options: Child traces linked to the parent task
mcq.why: Links keep the run navigable.

mcq.q: Which tools offer LLM-specific trace UIs and accept OpenTelemetry data?
mcq.why: They show prompts, responses, token costs and evaluations.

mcq.q: A tool times out once after 2 s and then succeeds in 240 ms. How much does the retry add?
mcq.why: The timeout is spent before the successful retry.
distractors: That is the retry's own time.

mcq.q: In the critical-path figure, which change cuts end-to-end time most with the default values?
options: Reducing the tool call by 20 ms
mcq.why: The longest span on the critical path offers the biggest saving.
distractors: BM25 is not on the critical path.

mcq.why: For AI services, measure them per stage and per model.

mcq.q: Why report latency percentiles rather than the mean?
options: LLM latency is skewed; the mean hides the slow tail users complain about
The mean is hard to compute
mcq.why: Report p50, p95 and p99.
distractors: It is easy; that is not the issue.

mcq.q: Which queue signal is the better alert?
mcq.why: Age directly measures delay.
distractors: Length can be high but fast.

mcq.q: A rise in schema-validation failures is often the first sign of…
mcq.why: Track errors by type.

mcq.q: Choose all the saturation signals the chapter lists.
mcq.why: Also connection pools and index node memory.

mcq.q: p50 is flat but p99 climbs from 6 s to 19 s while waiting sequences rise on one replica. What did the chapter find?
options: A long-context tenant sending 100k-token prompts that occupy KV cache
mcq.why: Per-tenant admission limits and a long-context pool fixed it.

mcq.q: Requests hang instead of failing. What does a low error rate tell you?
options: Little; hanging requests may not count as errors
mcq.why: Watch latency and queue age too.

mcq.q: Which latencies should be tracked separately for streaming LLM calls?
mcq.why: They have different causes (14.2).

mcq.q: In the percentile figure, as the tail gets heavier, what changes most?
mcq.why: The median barely moves.

mcq.q: Which describes availability as an SLI?
options: Successful requests ÷ valid requests, against the SLO
mcq.why: Measured from requests, not machines (15.2).

mcq.q: Where should token counts come from?
mcq.why: Record input, cached input, output and reasoning tokens per call.

mcq.q: Choose all the tags each call should carry for cost attribution.
options: The full prompt text as a label
mcq.why: Also a hashed user ID.

mcq.q: Which non-token costs should be included?
options: Embeddings, vector DB, GPU-hours and tool APIs
mcq.why: Allocate them by usage.

mcq.q: In the spend figure, grouping by token type shows output and uncached input dominate. What does that suggest?
options: Work on prompt caching and output length
mcq.why: Each grouping suggests different actions.

mcq.q: One tenant is 31% of spend. What is it useful for?
options: Billing, abuse detection and capacity forecasts
mcq.why: Tenant usage vs quota and contract.

mcq.q: GPU utilisation is 95% but cost per successful task is poor. What is the lesson?
options: Utilisation is not economics; measure cost per success
mcq.why: Busy GPUs can still produce failed tasks.

mcq.q: A task makes four model calls and two retries. What should cost reports show?
options: The full attributed cost of all calls and the outcome
mcq.why: Retries and extra calls are real cost.

mcq.q: Why record the price version with each usage record?
options: Prices change; you need the price that applied to compute cost correctly
mcq.why: Historic costs need historic prices.

mcq.q: Which self-hosted metric shows real cost efficiency?
options: Cost per million tokens actually served
mcq.why: Include idle hours.

mcq.q: Which token types should a usage record separate?
options: Input, cached input, output and reasoning tokens
mcq.why: They have different prices.

mcq.q: What is the weakness of head sampling?
options: It decides at the start, so it misses rare failures
mcq.why: Tail sampling decides after the trace completes.

mcq.q: Choose all the traces tail sampling should always keep.
options: Low quality scores and flagged safety events
mcq.why: Plus a random baseline of the rest.

mcq.q: Should metrics be sampled?
mcq.why: Metrics are cheap aggregates.

mcq.q: Always keep 3% (errors, slow, flagged) plus a 5% random sample of the rest. What share of traces is kept?
What should never be logged?
mcq.why: Prompts and outputs need per-field decisions; secrets are never logged.

mcq.q: Why alert on dropped-span and queue-full counters?
options: A silent pipeline looks exactly like a healthy, quiet system
mcq.why: Missing telemetry must be visible.

mcq.q: Which is a sensible retention example from the chapter?
options: Metrics 13 months, sampled traces 30 days, full content 7 days in a restricted store
mcq.why: Audit logs follow legal requirements.

mcq.q: Do deletion requests apply to telemetry?
options: Yes; they must reach telemetry too
mcq.why: Traces can contain personal data.
distractors: Audit logs follow their own rules.

mcq.q: Options for a prompt field in telemetry include…
options: Not recorded, hashed, redacted, or recorded in a restricted store with shorter retention
mcq.why: Choose per field.

mcq.q: LLM traces with content can be tens of KB each. What is the main consequence?
options: Storage and ingest must be budgeted, and content stripped or sampled
mcq.why: Telemetry costs are real.

mcq.q: How do you detect quality drift?
options: Continuous sampled evaluation plus input-distribution monitoring
mcq.why: Topics, languages, query lengths and retrieval score distributions.

mcq.q: Why record the response's model version in every trace?
options: Providers update models behind aliases; you need to see when it changed
mcq.why: Pin snapshots where offered and annotate dashboards on change.

mcq.q: How do you use delayed outcomes such as audits 45 days later?
options: Join them back to the original trace by ID
mcq.why: Then report accuracy per prompt and model version.

mcq.q: In the claims-triage example, what did the delayed audit reveal?
options: Prompt v14 had 3× the overturn rate of v13
mcq.why: Faster signals had not shown it.

mcq.q: What should you check about proxy signals?
options: That they track the real outcomes
mcq.why: Validate proxies against delayed outcomes.

mcq.q: In the 60-day figure, what caused gradual drift?
options: A new product line whose documents were never ingested
mcq.why: Gradual drift points to data gaps.

mcq.q: Negative ratings rose after the traffic mix changed. What should you check first?
options: Whether the mix of questions changed, before blaming the model
mcq.why: Input-distribution monitors separate mix shifts from regressions.

mcq.q: Which freshness signal suits time-sensitive domains?
options: Answers citing documents older than a set age
mcq.why: Plus ingestion lag and index staleness against the SLO.

mcq.q: What should happen on any model change?
mcq.why: Changes can break prompts and formats.

mcq.q: In the 60-day figure, what did the index migration do to groundedness?
mcq.why: Annotations show which events mattered.
distractors: That was the missing product line.

mcq.q: Why are production failures the most valuable evaluation data?
options: They are real and they were missed
mcq.why: Make the path from bad trace to test short.

mcq.q: Choose all the steps in the improvement flywheel.
options: Label the root cause and stage
Create an evaluation case and gate releases on it
mcq.why: Then fix the cause, deploy and monitor.

mcq.q: What should be fixed after a failure?
options: The root cause, not just the single example
mcq.why: e.g. improve parsing for that document type.

mcq.q: What must happen before production text becomes an evaluation case?
options: Redact personal data and get approval if content is sensitive
mcq.why: Raw customer conversations must not enter shared sets without review.

mcq.q: What does the release gate run?
options: The suite including the new cases and all old ones
mcq.why: See 8.6 and 18.3.

mcq.q: After deploying the fix, what should you check?
options: That the failure signal falls for that category
mcq.why: Close the loop.

mcq.q: Why add paraphrases to a new evaluation case?
options: So the fix generalises beyond one exact wording
mcq.why: One wording can be overfitted.

mcq.q: What tags should an evaluation case from production carry?
options: Links to the trace and the issue
mcq.why: Traceability to the original failure.

mcq.q: Over months, what does the flywheel turn the evaluation suite into?
options: A precise description of what users actually need
mcq.why: Real failures shape it.

mcq.q: Who should classify a failure's stage (retrieval, generation, tool, data)?
options: Reviewers in the triage queue, noting the correct behaviour
mcq.why: The stage guides the fix (8.5).
